lines.text: Watch how one full-back breaks a four-four-two. The Reds line up in a four-three-three, the Blues sit in a compact mid-block.
The right-back leaves the touchline and steps inside, next to the holding midfielder.
Now two strikers cannot screen two pivots. The ball goes inside, the six turns, and the eight receives between the lines.
When a centre-back steps out, five forwards against four defenders leaves the striker free. One pass, and he is through on goal.
Three at the back, two in the pivot, five in attack. That is the three-two-five, built from a simple full-back rotation.
Control the middle, and the block has nowhere to hide.
